articles.title: Getting started with {{name}}
articles.desc: Choose your language and get to know the main areas

steps.title: Choose your language
steps.text: Account icon (bottom left) → Settings (or Ctrl + .) → Language, pick a language and click Save.

steps.title: Get to know the sidebar
steps.text: Use New Chat to talk privately with the AI, Channels to work with your team, and Search to find earlier conversations.

articles.tip: In these guides, @Knight is an example name for the AI assistant; use the name of the assistant your administrator created.

articles.title: What are Channels, Group Channels and Direct Messages?
articles.desc: How the three channel types differ and why all three exist

steps.title: Channel
steps.text: The organization's official space for discussion, for example a department channel, a company-wide announcement channel or a large project channel. Administrators grant access to groups and users: Public means everyone in the system can see it, Private means only those granted access. Membership follows the groups, so people don't need to be invited one by one. Only administrators can create this type.

steps.title: Group Channel
steps.text: A working group that users set up themselves when needed, for example a project team, a daily-report group or a temporary task force. The creator invites each member and can make it Private so only members can see it. Both users and administrators can create it.

steps.title: Direct Message
steps.text: A private conversation between a few selected people, with no channel name needed. Use it for quick questions or private matters that the whole team doesn't need to see. Both users and administrators can create it.

steps.title: Why three types?
steps.text: Each type serves a different level of discussion and a different way of managing access. Channels are for official content, with access managed centrally by administrators so that not everyone creates company-wide channels that are hard to control and risk exposing data. Group Channels let teams set up their own workspace right away without waiting for an administrator. Direct Messages keep private exchanges out of shared channels so those don't get cluttered.

steps.title: Choosing the right type
steps.text: Announcements or department-wide discussion: use a Channel (ask an administrator to create it). A team project or daily reports: use a Group Channel. A quick question for one or two people: use a Direct Message.

articles.tip: Whichever type you use, when you ask the AI assistant in a channel or conversation, it only reads the content of that place.

articles.title: Channel types and creating channels
articles.desc: The three channel types and which ones you can create for your role

steps.title: Know the channel types
steps.text: There are three: Channel (official department or announcement channel), Group Channel (a working group users set up themselves) and Direct Message (a private conversation between a few people). See "What are Channels, Group Channels and Direct Messages?" for the differences.

steps.title: What you can create by role
steps.text: Users (user) can create Group Channels and Direct Messages. Administrators (admin) can create all three types: Channel, Group Channel and Direct Message.

steps.title: Open the channel list
steps.text: The channels you belong to appear under Channels in the left sidebar; click a channel name to open it.

steps.title: Choose the channel type
steps.text: Click + next to the Channels heading and choose the Channel Type. The list only shows the types you are allowed to create.

steps.title: Name it and choose members
steps.text: Group Channel: enter a Channel Name (for example project-a, daily-reports), pick the participants and make it Private if needed. Direct Message: just pick the participants. Channel (administrators): enter a name, set Public or Private and grant access to groups or users.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Click Create to start the conversation.

articles.tip: No Channel option when creating? That type is for administrators only; use a Group Channel or ask an administrator to create it. If you cannot see a channel you need, ask an administrator to add you.

images.caption: Creating a group channel or direct message

articles.title: Sending messages and replying in threads
articles.desc: Mention, reply, send files and find messages

steps.title: Send a message
steps.text: Type in the message box at the bottom of the channel and press Enter. Use Shift + Enter for a new line.

steps.title: Mention someone
steps.text: Type @ and pick the right person from the suggestions.

steps.title: Reply to a message
steps.text: Hover over a message → Reply. Your reply quotes the original message.

steps.title: Discuss in a thread
steps.text: Hover over a message → Reply in Thread. The thread opens in the right panel.

steps.title: Copy a message
steps.text: Hover over a message (including AI replies) → click the Copy icon.

steps.title: Send a file
steps.text: Click + in the message box and choose a file from your computer.

steps.title: Find older messages
steps.text: Click the magnifying glass at the top right of the channel.

articles.title: Asking the AI assistant in a channel
articles.desc: How to mention @Knight and read the result

steps.title: Open the right channel
steps.text: Go to the channel that holds the reports or information you want the AI to work with.

steps.title: Mention the assistant
steps.text: In the message box, type @, choose the AI assistant (for example Knight), then write your request and send it.

steps.title: Read the result
steps.text: The AI's answer appears in the thread of your message. Click the answer to open the thread on the right and see it in full.

articles.tip: In a channel, the AI only reads and searches the current channel; reports from other channels are not mixed in. For the AI to see the full channel history, ask in a new message in the main channel view, not inside a thread or by editing an old message.

images.caption: Type @ and choose the AI assistant
Click the AI's reply to see it in full in the thread

articles.title: Report summaries and progress tracking
articles.desc: Summaries by day, person and work item

steps.title: Choose a time range
steps.text: The AI understands "today", "yesterday", "this week" and specific dates in day/month format. It only uses messages sent in the requested period and skips messages that say they report on another day.

steps.title: Be specific
steps.text: Ask by person, work item, completion rate or blocked issues, or ask for a table with the columns you need.

steps.title: Use Work progress
steps.text: In a channel, click the Work progress button to have the AI summarize progress. Click Update now to have it summarize new messages and show the result right away.

articles.example: @Knight make a progress table: owner, work item, % complete, blockers
articles.tip: More examples: "summarize my reports for 11/11", "who has not sent a report today?", "compare today's progress with yesterday", "summarize this week's reports as a table: Date | Person | Done | Pending". To summarize several channels at once, use a chat outside the channel.

images.caption: A weekly report summarized as a table
The Update now button in the Work progress panel
The Work progress panel in a channel

articles.title: Asking about earlier messages
articles.desc: Summarize, recall and follow up on past discussions

steps.title: Ask about past discussions
steps.text: Mention @Knight and ask about a time range or topic, for example "what did I report?" or "summarize the discussion since this morning".

steps.title: Focus on one message
steps.text: Click Reply on that message, then mention @Knight in your reply.

steps.title: Follow up on an AI reply
steps.text: Keep typing in the thread that holds the reply. The AI remembers the original question and its earlier answers in the thread.

articles.tip: The AI understands "today", "yesterday", "this week" and specific dates in day/month format.

images.caption: Asking the AI about earlier discussions in a channel

articles.title: Exporting reports as PDF, Word or Excel
articles.desc: Have the AI create a file you can download right in the conversation

steps.title: In a channel
steps.text: Mention @Knight and state the format you need. The AI uses the Terminal automatically if you have access to it.

steps.title: In a private chat
steps.text: Select the Terminal (ncs-terminal) in the message box before sending your request.

steps.title: Download the file
steps.text: The file is attached right below the AI's reply. Click it to preview or download.

articles.example: @Knight create this week's report for this channel as a PDF
articles.tip: If the AI only replies with text and attaches no file, your account may not have Terminal access. Contact an administrator.

articles.title: Sending files for the AI to review
articles.desc: Review PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint files and images

steps.title: Attach a file
steps.text: Click + in the message box and choose a file. Supported: images (PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF), PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx, .csv), PowerPoint (.pptx) and text (.txt, .md, .html).

steps.title: Wait for processing
steps.text: After uploading, wait a few seconds until the content has been read before asking the AI.

steps.title: Ask the AI about the file
steps.text: Mention the AI and name the file and the task. The AI picks files in this order: files attached to your request → files in the message you Reply to → files in the thread → otherwise the 5 newest files in the channel.

articles.example: @Knight summarize the PowerPoint presentation, one line per slide
articles.tip: When a channel has many files, the surest way is to Reply to the message that holds the file and mention the AI there. Save old formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt) as .docx, .xlsx, .pptx first. Reading images requires an assistant with Vision capability.

images.caption: Attaching a file and asking the AI
The AI summarizes the file

articles.title: Tracing sources
articles.desc: Check where information in an AI answer came from

steps.title: Ask the AI to cite sources
steps.text: When sending a request, ask the AI to state the sender, time and file name for each point.

steps.title: Verify in the channel
steps.text: Use the channel's magnifying glass to find the original message by keyword, sender name or the file name the AI mentioned.

articles.example: @Knight summarize my progress today, with the time and file name for each point

images.caption: The AI states the sender, time and file name for each point

articles.title: Private chat and asking across channels

steps.title: Start a private chat
steps.text: Click New Chat in the left sidebar. A private chat is visible only to you and is saved in your chat list.

steps.title: Choose the assistant
steps.text: Select the AI assistant at the top of the chat (for example Knight) and type your question. No @ is needed outside channels; attach files with the + button.

steps.title: Ask across channels
steps.text: The AI can search all channels you are a member of, which helps to summarize several channels or find a discussion when you don't remember where it was.

articles.tip: Results only include channels you are a member of. If you need information from another channel, ask an administrator to add you to it.

images.caption: Private chat with the AI
Asking the AI about the channels you belong to

articles.title: Searching the knowledge base
articles.desc: Ask the AI based on the company's shared documents

steps.title: What a knowledge base is
steps.text: A place where administrators keep shared documents such as procedures, policies and technical documents. When you ask, the AI finds the relevant passages and answers with the sources.

steps.title: Ask in a private chat
steps.text: Click New Chat, type # in the message box and choose the knowledge base, then type your question and send it.

steps.title: Ask in a channel
steps.text: If an administrator has attached the knowledge base to the AI assistant, just mention @Knight as usual; the assistant looks it up when the question is related.

steps.title: Check the sources
steps.text: Click the sources shown below the answer to see the original passage.

articles.example: @Knight according to the procedure, how long are residential proxies issued for?
articles.tip: Be specific and use keywords from the documents (procedure name, form code, project name). To summarize a whole long document, send the file in the chat instead. If # does not show the knowledge base you need, you do not have access yet; contact an administrator.

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.desc: Missing channels, assistant, history, files or knowledge bases

steps.title: A channel is missing
steps.text: Reload the page (F5). If it is still missing, ask an administrator to add you to the channel.

steps.title: The AI assistant does not appear after @
steps.text: You may not have access to this model yet. Contact an administrator.

steps.title: The AI ignores reports from other channels
steps.text: In a channel, the AI only reads the current channel. To summarize several channels, use a chat outside the channel.

steps.title: The AI answer misses channel history
steps.text: Ask the AI in a new message in the main channel view, not inside a thread or by editing an old message.

steps.title: The AI reads the wrong file or none
steps.text: Wait a few seconds until the file is processed, or Reply to the message that holds the file and mention the AI there. For old formats, save as .docx, .xlsx, .pptx and send again.

steps.title: The AI cannot read an image
steps.text: This needs an assistant with Vision capability. Contact an administrator if the current one does not support it.

steps.title: # does not show a knowledge base
steps.text: You do not have access to that knowledge base yet. Contact an administrator.

steps.title: The AI answers from outdated documents
steps.text: The documents in the knowledge base have not been updated. Ask an administrator to upload the new version.

steps.title: Forgot your password
steps.text: Contact an administrator to have your password reset.

articles.title: Creating user accounts
articles.desc: Add accounts, assign roles, import from CSV and approve pending users

steps.title: Open the admin area
steps.text: Account icon (bottom left) → Admin Panel. Only administrator accounts see this item.

steps.title: Add a user
steps.text: Go to Users → click Add User.

steps.title: Enter the details
steps.text: On the Form tab, choose the Role and enter the Name, Email and a temporary Password. Roles: admin (full access), user (chat, channels and permitted models), pending (awaiting approval, cannot use the system yet).

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Click Save, then send the email and temporary password to the user. To create many accounts at once, use the CSV Import tab: download the template, fill in the list and upload it.

articles.tip: Self-registered accounts and users signing in with Microsoft may start as pending. Approve them by clicking their role in the Users list and changing it to user.

images.caption: Admin Panel → Users
The add-user form

articles.title: Configuring the AI assistant and its system prompt
articles.desc: Define its tasks, answer rules and who can use it

steps.title: Open the model settings
steps.text: Admin Panel → Settings → Models, and choose the assistant to configure (for example Knight).

steps.title: Write the System Prompt
steps.text: The system prompt is the assistant's "job description" and applies to every question. State its tasks (summarize reports, track progress, review files) and rules: answer concisely, name the sender and time, never guess figures, name people whose reports are missing, and end each summary with "Points to watch".

steps.title: Set access
steps.text: Set Access to Public or choose groups so users can call the assistant.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Click Save & Update to apply.

articles.tip: You can add the report format you want to the system prompt, for example: "Present it as a table with the columns: Owner | Work item | Status | Notes". Also state that it must not claim to be another model, and must not say a file was created unless the tool reported success.

images.caption: Configuring the AI assistant's system prompt

articles.title: Enabling, creating channels and managing members
articles.desc: Turn on channels, create all three channel types and add or remove members

steps.title: Enable channels
steps.text: Admin Panel → Settings, under Admin choose System → General settings, turn on Channels and click Save. If Channels does not appear in the sidebar, reload the page (F5).

steps.title: Choose the channel type
steps.text: In the sidebar click + next to Channels. Administrators can create all three types: Channel (shared department or announcement channel with access managed centrally by groups and users), Group Channel (invited members, can be Private) and Direct Message (a private conversation between a few people). Regular users can only create Group Channels and Direct Messages.

steps.title: Set it up and create
steps.text: Enter a Channel Name (for example project-a, daily-reports). For a Channel: set Public or Private and grant access to groups and users. For a Group Channel or Direct Message: pick the participants. Click Create.

steps.title: Add or remove members
steps.text: Open the channel and click the members icon at the top right (a person with the member count) or the ⋯ menu → Edit Channel.

steps.title: Update
steps.text: Add users or groups, remove people who left, then click Update.

articles.tip: Use the Channel type for departments or announcements that need central access control, and let users create Group Channels for their projects. Check the Public / Private setting before creating a channel for internal data.

images.caption: Enabling channels in General settings
Creating a channel
The members icon at the top of a channel
Add or remove members, then click Update

articles.title: Creating a knowledge base and adding documents
articles.desc: Create a knowledge base in the Workspace and upload documents

steps.title: Open Knowledge
steps.text: In the left sidebar, click Workspace and choose the Knowledge tab.

steps.title: Create a knowledge base
steps.text: Click +. In "What are you working on?" enter the name; in "What are you trying to achieve?" briefly describe its purpose. Choose the initial Visibility and click Create Knowledge.

steps.title: Add documents
steps.text: On the knowledge base page, click Add Content and choose: Upload files, Upload directory, Sync directory (updates new or changed files), Add text content or Add webpage.

steps.title: Test it
steps.text: Wait until the files are processed, then use Test Query on the knowledge base page to ask a sample question.

articles.tip: Prefer several small knowledge bases by topic over one large one. When a document changes, delete the old file and upload the new one (or use Sync directory); otherwise the AI keeps answering from the old content. Save .doc, .xls, .ppt files in the newer formats before uploading.

articles.title: Knowledge base access
articles.desc: Choose Public or Private and grant Read or Write access

steps.title: Open access settings
steps.text: On the knowledge base page, click the Access button at the top right.

steps.title: Choose the Visibility
steps.text: Public: every user can search it. Private: only the creator and the users or groups in the access list.

steps.title: Grant access
steps.text: For Private, click Add Access, choose users or groups, then choose Read (search the knowledge base) or Write (search and add or remove documents).

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Changes are saved immediately and a confirmation appears.

articles.tip: Grant access by group, so staff changes only need one update to the group.

articles.title: Using knowledge bases with the AI assistant
articles.desc: Call a knowledge base with # or attach it to the assistant

steps.title: Call it when needed
steps.text: In a private chat, type # and choose the knowledge base, then ask your question.

steps.title: Attach it to the assistant
steps.text: Admin Panel → Settings → Models, choose the assistant (for example Knight). Under Knowledge, click Select Knowledge and choose the knowledge base.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Click Save & Update. From then on the assistant consults the knowledge base whenever it answers, including in channels, and users do not need to type #.

articles.example: @Knight according to the procedure, how long are residential proxies issued for, and can they be extended?
articles.tip: Everyone who can use the assistant can receive information from the knowledge bases attached to it; keep sensitive documents in a Private knowledge base searched only with #. To make the AI answer only from the documents, add to the System Prompt: "Answer only from the knowledge base documents; if the information is not there, say so clearly."
